connections.observation: `s001` names injustice through four nouns of disorder (στάσιν, πολυπραγμοσύνην, ἀλλοτριοπραγμοσύνην, ἐπανάστασιν); `s002` specifies that disorder as what naturally should serve (δουλεύειν) attempting to rule (ἄρχῃ). Held together, the uprising of a part against the whole is made concrete: the servant-part attempts mastery, interrupting natural reciprocal rule.

`s001` defines injustice through internal disorder of three psychic elements; `s003` gathers ἀδικίαν, ἀκολασίαν, δειλίαν, ἀμαθίαν under πᾶσαν κακίαν with συλλήβδην. The conjunction shows that the four individual vices named are not separate pathologies but manifestations of a single structural disorder—the rebellion and confusion of psychic parts.

`s002` contrasts ruling and being enslaved in the definition of injustice; `s007` contrasts κρατεῖν τε καὶ κρατεῖσθαι ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων (health) with ἄρχειν τε καὶ ἄρχεσθαι ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου (disease). The shift from ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων to ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου makes visible what injustice destroys: reciprocal mastery becomes alien rule when what should serve rules instead.

`s004` establishes the body/soul parallel through ἐν σώματι / ἐν ψυχῇ; `s005` transfers ἐμποιέω from bodily health to psychic justice three times; `s006` repeats κατὰ φύσιν / παρὰ φύσιν exactly for body then soul. Together, these three signals enact the analogy as a syntactic movement: the same verb, the same preposition-pairs, the same locative structure cross from body to soul, making justice visible as psychic health by performing the transfer through repeated forms.

`s008` identifies virtue with ὑγίεια, κάλλος, εὐεξία and vice with νόσος, αἶσχος, ἀσθένεια; `s009` contrasts καλὰ ἐπιτηδεύματα leading to ἀρετή with αἰσχρά leading to κακία. Held together, the triad κάλλος/αἶσχος in `s008` is enacted through practices named καλά/αἰσχρά in `s009`: beauty and ugliness of soul are acquired through beautiful and ugly pursuits, completing the somatic image with action.

`s010` frames the remaining question with two forms of concealment: whether justice escapes notice (λανθάνῃ) and whether injustice escapes punishment (μὴ διδῷ δίκην); `s012` lists σιτίων, ποτῶν, πλούτου, ἀρχῆς as insufficient when the body is destroyed. The conjunction makes visible what the question of concealment concerns: whether external goods and impunity can sustain life when internal psychic nature is corrupted, just as food and power cannot sustain a destroyed body.

`s011` records Glaucon calling the inquiry γελοῖον and Socrates echoing the word back; `s013` describes the argument as an ascent (ἀναβεβήκαμεν) to a lookout point (σκοπιά). Held together, the transition is made perceptible: Socrates accepts the inquiry as ridiculous yet simultaneously recasts it as spatial elevation, turning acknowledgment of absurdity into a vantage from which to survey what follows.

`s013` positions the argument at a lookout point (σκοπιά) reached by ascent (ἀναβεβήκαμεν); `s014` clusters visual vocabulary (ἴδῃς, θέας, φαίνεται, κατιδεῖν) around the forms of vice. The conjunction shows that elevation in argument becomes literal sight: from the height, forms become θέας ἄξια—worth looking at—and the turn to the five constitutions is enacted as inspection from above.

`s015` contrasts ἓν εἶδος τῆς ἀρετῆς with ἄπειρα τῆς κακίας, narrowed to τέτταρα worth mentioning; `s016` announces πέντε constitutions and πέντε soul-types with ὅσοι … τοσοῦτοι. The numerical shift from one/unlimited/four to five is made visible: the single form of virtue and four notable forms of vice yield five total types when virtue is counted with the four vicious constitutions as parallel cases.

`s015` names ἓν εἶδος τῆς ἀρετῆς despite ἄπειρα forms of κακία; `s017` names the good constitution twice—βασιλεία and ἀριστοκρατία—yet counts it as ἓν εἶδος. Held together, unity proves flexible: virtue has one form yet bears two names depending on whether one or several rule, and the section preserves the tension between numerical singularity and dual naming without resolution.

`s001` defines injustice as rebellion of a part against the whole, meddling, and faction among three psychic elements; `s018` closes with τροφή and παιδεία as the guarantee that rulers will not disturb worthy laws. The conjunction makes visible what prevents the disorder named at the opening: the rearing and education traversed in prior argument secure that psychic parts remain ordered and that rulers formed this way will not enact στάσις or πολυπραγμοσύνη in the city.

`s006` repeats κατὰ φύσιν / παρὰ φύσιν exactly for body then soul; `s007` repeats κρατεῖν τε καὶ κρατεῖσθαι ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων then shifts to ἄρχειν τε καὶ ἄρχεσθαι ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου. Together, these parallels enact the nature/against-nature opposition not only through preposition but through pronoun: ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων (by one another) is natural reciprocity; ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου (one thing by another) is alien imposition, and the shift in reciprocal pronoun embodies what it means to act παρὰ φύσιν.

elements.context: τροφῇ τε καὶ παιδείᾳ χρησάμενος ᾗ διήλθομεν

new_signals.observation: The perfect forms διεληλύθαμεν (twice) and διήλθομεν recur, marking completed traversal: the constitution and the natures of justice and injustice have been gone through, and the final reference anchors τροφή and παιδεία to that completed path.

elements.context: βιωτὸν ἄρα ἔσται, ἐάνπερ τις ποιῇ ὃ ἂν βουληθῇ

new_signals.observation: βιωτόν appears twice in Glaucon's objection: life is not βιωτόν when the body's nature is destroyed, yet the question asks if it will be βιωτόν when the soul's nature is destroyed but one does whatever one wishes. The repeated adjective frames the absurdity through parallel construction.

elements.context: οὔτε γὰρ ἂν πλείους οὔτε εἷς ἐγγενόμενοι

new_signals.observation: ἐγγίγνομαι appears as genitive singular absolute (ἐγγενομένου) when naming the constitution, then as nominative plural participle (ἐγγενόμενοι) when asserting that neither one nor many rulers so formed would disturb laws. The shift from singular to plural participle enacts the flexibility of the single constitution under varied leadership.
